item.title: Why the mean of original sample calculated by boot differs from my manual calculation?
item.description:
I use the boot package for bootstrapping:
bootstrap_mean <- function(data, indices) { return(mean(data[indices], na.rm = TRUE)) } # generate bootstrapped samples boot_with <- boot(entries_with$mood_value, statistic = bootstrap_mean, R = 1000) boot_without <- boot(entries_without$mood_value, statistic = bootstrap_mean, R = 1000)
However, upon closer inspection the original sample's mean differs from the mean I can calculate "by hand":
> boot_with
Bootstrap Statistics : original bias std. error t1* 2.614035 -0.005561404 0.1602418
> mean(entries_with$mood_value, na.rm = TRUE) [1] 2.603175
As you can see, **original** says the mean should equal to 2.614035 according to boot. But my calculation says 2.603175. Why do these calculations differ? Unless I'm misinterpreting what **original** means in the boot package?
Here's what's inside my `entries_with$mood_value` array so you can check by yourself:
> entries_with[["mood_value"]] [1] 2 4 1 2 1 2 4 5 2 4 1 1 4 3 4 2 4 1 2 1 2 1 2 2 2 2 2 1 4 2 3 2 3 5 4 4 2 2 [39] 4 2 2 2 4 1 5 2 2 1 4 2 3 3 4 4 2 2 2 4 4 2 2 2 4
